title: Recipe 36 — Cloud Deploy (three tiers, rendered before anything is applied)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Terraform for the cluster, Kustomize for the workload, one config object that renders both.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Type a harness to deploy
beats.cue: “Cloud deploy doesn't care which shape it is — it ships whatever the compiler emitted.”

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check first. Never ship a bundle you haven't proved boots.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

groups.title: Beat 2 · the three tiers, rendered not applied

beats.label: Render the dev tier on AWS
beats.cue: “The recipe's own CLI line. Note the skips: terraform-init, terraform-apply, kubectl-apply. Nothing is provisioned — this is a render.”
beats.command: crewhaus cloud deploy --provider aws --region us-east-1 --tier dev > live/aws-dev.txt 2>&1

verify.note: renders the module set and reports the apply steps it skipped

beats.label: Read what it rendered
beats.cue: “A working directory, a module set, and three skipped verbs. That gap is where your change review goes.”

beats.label: Render the same thing on GCP
beats.cue: “Same tier, different provider — google_container_cluster instead of aws_eks_cluster, and the workload overlay is untouched.”
beats.command: crewhaus cloud deploy --provider gcp --region us-central1 --tier dev > live/gcp-dev.txt 2>&1

verify.note: the provider swap is a flag, not a rewrite

beats.label: Render the prod tier
beats.cue: “Tier is the only thing that changes the replica counts, the node sizes, and the HA posture.”
beats.command: crewhaus cloud deploy --provider aws --region us-east-1 --tier production > live/aws-prod.txt 2>&1

beats.label: Diff dev against prod
beats.cue: “One flag, and here is precisely what it bought. Read this before you ever type --apply.”
beats.command: diff live/aws-dev.txt live/aws-prod.txt > live/tier.diff; test -f live/tier.diff

beats.label: Read the delta
beats.cue: “Infrastructure review is a diff review. Same as everything else here.”

beats.label: Type the config the CLI wraps
beats.cue: “defaultCloudConfig — the recipe's TypeScript entry point. The CLI is a thin shell over this.”

beats.label: Type the orchestrator call
beats.cue: “deployCloud takes that config and walks the same steps the CLI just skipped.”

beats.label: Open them side by side
beats.cue: “If you need this in CI rather than a terminal, this is the surface you call.”

groups.title: One more thing · actually applying it

beats.label: Apply for real
beats.cue: [manual] “Everything so far was a render. Applying needs cloud credentials, a real cluster, and a human who has read the diff.”
beats.command: crewhaus cloud deploy --provider aws --region us-east-1 --tier production --apply

verify.note: provisions real infrastructure; needs an AWS credential chain and deliberate human sign-off

beats.label: Tear it down
beats.cue: [manual] “The recipe pairs every deploy with its teardown. Demo clusters that outlive the demo are how cloud bills happen.”
